fields.h1: Build a Webinar Landing Page That Gets People to Show Up
fields.hero_description: Describe the session and where it runs. Emergent builds the webinar landing page and registers each sign-up with your webinar tool. Every registrant also lands in a table you own.
fields.features_heading: What Webinar Landing Pages Need to Work
fields.features_subheading: The page sells the session. What sits behind the form decides whether the people who register get a link and turn up.
fields.feature_1:
A personal join link for every sign-up

The form sends each registration to Zoom, or to any webinar tool with an API, and stores the join link it returns. The confirmation email carries that link and nobody else's.
fields.feature_2:
A calendar file on the confirmation

Ask for an .ics file on the confirmation email, with the join link written into the event notes. Opening the file adds the session to the registrant's calendar, link and all.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders timed to the start

Reminder emails go out a day before and an hour before, each with the same personal link. Anyone who registers after the first send still gets the hour-before email.
fields.feature_4:
A registrant table you can query

Every sign-up becomes a row with the name, work email, join link and time of registration. Filter it before the session, or sync new rows to HubSpot or any CRM with an API.
fields.feature_5:
Date changes made by message

Tell Emergent the session moved to next Thursday, and the page and its reminder schedule both change. People who already registered get an email with the new start time.
fields.feature_6:
Page and registrants exported as code

The page, its form, and the registrant table export to your GitHub on paid plans. Publish on Emergent under a custom domain, which uses credits, or host the code yourself.

fields.usecase_heading: Webinar Pages for Four Kinds of Session
fields.tab_content_1:
The start time, read in each visitor's own zone

Kestrel Payroll schedules its product demo for Thursdays at 11 AM Pacific. A finance lead who opens the page in New York sees 2:00 PM Eastern, taken from her browser, with the Pacific time in small type underneath. Her confirmation email repeats the time in Eastern.
fields.tab_content_2:
When the live hour ends, the recording takes its place

Fieldnote ran its survey design session live for 412 registrants. Once the hour was over, the headline switched to Watch the Recording, with the form left where it was. Another 268 people have signed up since then, each tagged replay in the table and emailed the recording link.
fields.tab_content_3:
Four sessions on one form, each with its own seat count

New Plumtree customers learn the bookkeeping app in four weekly sessions and tick only the ones they need. Each session caps at 100 seats. Bank Feeds filled first, and its checkbox now reads Join the Waitlist, with waitlist sign-ups saved apart from confirmed seats.
fields.tab_content_4:
86 questions, grouped by topic for the moderator

Every registrant for Northwind People's panel on hiring without a recruiter can ask one question on the form. By the morning of the panel, 86 had come in. At 8 AM, the moderator, Lena Okafor, gets a direct message in Slack with them grouped by topic. Pay ranges lead with 31.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Webinar Landing Page
fields.howto_description: A webinar page asks a busy person to give up an hour on a fixed day. These steps cover the pitch first, then the form and the tracking that tell you whether it worked.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Lead with what attendees leave with
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the time and length up top
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show the speakers and the agenda
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only for what you will use
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write the headline as the result of the hour: close the books in two days, not the name of the series. A subhead names who the session is for, such as finance leads at companies with one bookkeeper, which lets the wrong visitors leave early.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Visitors check the slot before anything else. Show the weekday, the start time and the length next to the headline, and say whether there is live Q&A. If a recording will follow, say so there for the people who cannot make it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each speaker a photo and one line on what they will cover. An agenda with minute marks, such as open questions at minute 40, tells a visitor whether the hour is worth it and when it is safe to join late.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A name and a work email are enough to send a join link. Add a field only when something depends on it, such as company size deciding which rep follows up. Fields nobody reads after the session belong off the form.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Mark it up as an online event
fields.howto_step_5_des: Google's Event structured data has a setting for online sessions: eventAttendanceMode set to OnlineEventAttendanceMode, with a VirtualLocation holding the page URL. Give the start date a time zone offset, because there is no venue for search engines to read it from.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Tag every link that promotes it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add utm_source and utm_campaign to each link pointing at the page, the speaker's LinkedIn post included. Saving those values with each registrant shows which channel filled the seats, instead of a single total that hides where people came from.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the session, export attendance from the webinar tool and match it to the registrant table by email. Show-up rate per channel matters more than sign-ups: a list that registers well and never attends needs a different reminder or a different offer.

plan.angle: Ranking for this term are example roundups (Instapage, HubSpot, Swipe Pages), template galleries (Leadpages, Behance, Dribbble, Pinterest) and two platform posts (BigMarker, Zoom). They judge a webinar page by its layout and stop at the sign-up button. This page defines the term for the AI Overview, then shows four working webinar pages by format, each with what happens after the click: the start time in the visitor's own zone, a personal join link from the webinar platform's API, the switch to a replay, session picks and questions collected for the panel, plus a how-to grounded in Google, Zoom and calendar standards.
tab_stories: Kestrel Payroll's Thursday demo page shows a visitor in New York 2:00 PM Eastern instead of the 11 AM Pacific the team scheduled, and each sign-up is registered in Zoom through its API so the confirmation carries a personal join link.
When Fieldnote's live session on survey design ends, the same URL turns into a replay page, the form now unlocks the recording, and every new sign-up is tagged replay in the registrant table.
Plumtree's four-part onboarding series runs on one page where new customers tick the sessions they want, and the table counts seats per session against a 100-seat cap with a waitlist after that.
Northwind People's HR panel asks registrants for one question on the form, groups the 86 questions by topic and sends the moderator the top themes the morning of the panel.
